newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lanka rupee ends shade firm in ranged trade.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka rupee ends shade firm in ranged trade.

text.p: The Sri Lanka rupee closed slightly higher on Monday after moving in a tight range, hedged in by profit-taking and by borrowing from a state bank, dealers said.
The rupee closed at 56.72 to the dollar after opening at 56.75. The currency closed at 56.80 on Friday.
"Profit-taking brought the dollar down to 56.66, but pushed it back up to 56.72 on limited buying by a state bank," said a Standard Chartered dealer.
The U.S. unit has firm support at around 56.65, but the top side should be held near 56.80 due to limited commercial demand, said the dealer.
Overnight call money closed at 13.5 percent with the market very liquid due to a state bank lending, dealers said.
